Sign in

The Sheet asks who you are before it sends or receives anything. Pick your name and enter the 4-digit PIN the owner gave you.
Later keeps you recording — trees stay on this phone and go up once you sign in. Forgotten PIN? The owner can give you a new one from the Sheet.

Cruiser & ID settings

Pick your name so every tree you record is attributed to you. The list comes from the Sheet — new crew are added there by the owner, who gives each person their PIN.
Signed in
Your name is the one you signed in with. Sign out to switch.
Shared with the whole crew once you save.

Office settings replacement cost, tree value, project type
Per replacement tree, from the Region's Tree Removal Offsetting table. One rate for every tree since May 2025 — the deciduous and coniferous split was dropped. The Region reviews this figure, so confirm it for the job.
These are sent up to the Sheet's Settings tab when you change them, because the handover package is built there and needs them to fill its TREE_VAL column. Changed with no signal, they go up on the next sync.
A condition left blank produces no tree value at all, rather than a guessed one — a wrong factor is a wrong dollar figure in a submitted report. Good and Satisfactory are set from a real report table; fill the rest in when you have them.
Remembered per project. TPP adds tree number, tag, location, proposed action and long-term impact.
Height always uses the Aurora equation, so it stays comparable either way.

Legend

Choose what the tree symbols say, rename anything, put related layers under a heading, and give a group one colour so a dozen servicing lines read as one entry. What a sheet actually prints is still only what that sheet carries.
Trees
Tree locations draws every tree as one symbol — for a plan that shows where the trees are, not their condition. The others colour each tree by that field. Same setting as Layers → Colour trees by on the map.
The key prints Tree locations — rename it under Every legend item below if you want other words.
Automatic prints “LEGEND — HEALTH” and so on when the trees are coloured by a field, and just “LEGEND” for tree locations.
Counted from what is on that sheet, so a sheet carrying 40 m of fence does not say 340 m.

Plan versions

A version is everything that shapes the document — wording, branding, layer symbology, the legend, the chosen standard drawings, the notes and arrows, and what the plan draws. Save one and every device on the project can bring in exactly that arrangement, change it, and save a new one. Nothing is ever overwritten.
It is a recipe, not an archive. The trees are not copied into it — they live on the Sheet and are the live job, so a version brought in months later draws the plan the old way from today's trees.
—
Ready to hand over?
Four ticks and anybody on this project can produce the same document. The one button above does all of it — you do not have to send anything separately.
Picking a project up on another device
1. Set Showing to this project.
2. Menu → Load trees from Sheet.
3. Come back here and tap Bring this in on the version you want. It fetches the layers and the report by itself.
4. Menu → Assemble the final document.
Versions

Project files

The two things the project setup cannot carry: the reference layer geometry and the pages of uploaded PDFs. They go to a Drive folder for this project, so a second device can pick them up instead of loading the zip and the report again.
—
Leave this on. It is what puts a layer you loaded here in front of everybody else on the project, without anybody having to remember to. One file at a time, layers first, in the background. Turn it off only on a phone you are paying for data on and have just loaded something large onto.
Leave that off on a phone in the field — a site plan and a thirty-page report are tens of megabytes. The app always checks and tells you what is missing; downloading is your decision unless you turn this on.

House standard

One saved setup that every new project starts from, on any device. Save it once from a job that is set up the way you want; after that a new project arrives already wearing your wording, your logo, your label style, your layer and fence symbology, your sheet size and your appraisal rates.
—
—
Saving overwrites the standard for everybody. Applying it to a project replaces that project's wording and styling with the standard's — the trees, the photographs and the tables are untouched.

Layers

—
Reference layers are for context — parcels, streets, boundaries, and a GPX track log of where the crew walked. They are drawn and labelled but never edited; ⬇ on any layer sends it back out as a shapefile or GeoJSON. To bring in trees you will edit, use Menu → Import tree points.

Copy fields into new trees

—
When you tap a feature on this layer and choose ＋ Tree here, these attributes are copied into the new tree. Leave any as “— none —” to fill it in yourself.

What is this layer for?

—
A parcel, street or park layer is used to fill tree fields automatically — far more accurate than looking the address up online.
—

Labels

—
The outline behind the text follows the colour — dark behind light text, light behind dark — so a label reads over an aerial either way. Units are added to the fields that are measurements, and never to a tree number.

Typed once and kept on this phone. Only the top two boxes normally change between jobs — the rest carry forward to the next plan.
Printed above the plant list. Blank lines start a new paragraph; a line beginning Timing: or Watering: prints with its lead word in bold.
Drawn in the Prepared by box on every sheet.

Standard detail drawings

The library is shared — added once, on every device, for every future job. Each page of a PDF becomes its own drawing. Tick the ones this project's document should carry.
Tap any drawing to see the full page. Recover drawings stored on this device if the list has lost them.

Layer name & legend

—
Two numbers, not one: a servicing line wants a solid edge over a barely-there fill, a grass restoration area wants the reverse. Both carry through to the plan sheet. Fill applies to polygons only.
The pattern prints on the plan as well as the map. Two lines on the same alignment are told apart by pattern when the drawing is photocopied and the colours go.
Off. Turn it on only for a plan printed over a dark air photo, where the colour alone is hard to pick out. Over a survey base leave it off — it prints as a white band either side of the line, and on two lines sharing one alignment it covers the colour of the line underneath.
Keeps the colour you set for the group and gives every layer in it a different pattern — solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot and so on — so the key identifies each one. The patterns go on the drawing too, not just the key.
Turn it off for base information that belongs on the drawing but not in the key.

Lines from a layer

—
Each line becomes a protection-plan line on this project, drawn on the map and on the site plan, exported with the fences and sent to the Sheet. Lengths are re-measured from the geometry.

Notes & arrows on the map

Anything on the plan that is not a tree or a fence — “proposed driveway”, “shed to be removed”, an arrow at the corner in question. They belong to this project and print on the site plan sheets.
The size is the height of the letters on the printed sheet, so a note set to 0.14 in comes out 0.14 in whatever scale the plan is drawn at. The map shows an approximation of it.

Appendix A — tree photographs

A document of its own, one photograph to a page, captioned so every picture can be found in Schedule A.
The tree number is always first and cannot be removed: it is the only thing tying a photograph to a row in Schedule A, and a photograph that cannot be looked up is one nobody can act on.

This device against the Sheet

—
Reads the Sheet and lines it up against this device, record by record and field by field — the trees, the fences and plantings, the notes and arrows, and the synced marks. Looking changes nothing. It tells you what differs and which button puts it right, and where it can put something right itself the button is here in the report and says how many it would touch.

What to show on the map

—
Leave both empty for every tree. This is what the map, Schedule A, Table 1, the compensation table and the photographs all report on — so a phase reported on today does not carry last month’s trees with it.
—
Nothing is being left out.
A tree matching any of these is off the map, out of the numbering and out of every table — one answer, so they cannot disagree. Condition ratings are the usual ones (Removed, Stump), but any field will do.
Only what is on this phone is listed. Use “Load trees from Sheet” to bring another project down first.

Find trees

—
The search covers what the Showing filter is set to and nothing else, so another project cannot be edited by accident.

Update from an edited file

—
Nothing is created and nothing is deleted. Trees already here are corrected from the file; rows that match no tree are reported and ignored; trees the file says nothing about are left as they are.
Only trees that are showing can be matched, so another project cannot be written to by accident.
A blank cell leaves the tree's value alone — it never clears it. Tree ID, project and the photo columns are never written.
The change goes on the undo stack and syncs to the Sheet — the same rows, changed, not new ones.

Selected trees

—
A tree in no parcel is in the road allowance, so it is Public; a tree inside one is on private land, so it is Private. Shared ownership is never guessed — a boundary tree is a judgement about a stem straddling a line, and a parcel fabric is not accurate enough to make a claim about somebody's property. Trees with no position, or with no parcel layer to test against, are left alone.
Subject property and adjacent property are both private land, so both become Private; road allowance becomes Public; shared / boundary becomes Shared ownership. Only trees still carrying an old value are touched, it goes on the undo stack, and you can change any of them afterwards.
This field can hold several values on one tree. Setting it here replaces whatever combination each tree has with the one value chosen. Undo puts them all back.
They go to the Deleted tab of the Sheet, which is the way back. This is not on the undo stack.
